answer: Proof-of-personhood checks that expire each epoch are the mechanism I would rely on. Each new key must pass a fresh, single-use verification tied to one human, and that pass dies quickly. A Sybil farm cannot stockpile them, so it must re-pass for every identity every epoch, and cost scales linearly with account count. An added signal, the rate of concurrent passes, flags a sudden tide of near-identical submissions as one operator. No farm outlasts that tide without paying fresh per-account costs each round, making mass identity creation an ivory-tower exercise in wasted capital.
